summary: Accepted ADR on renderer policy dated 2026-07-05. Context: shell and then-current surfaces were vanilla TS plus DOM with five runtime dependencies and one compiled exe per ADR-001 and ADR-003, while roadmap chat surfaces M4 Table Read and agent packages are classically React-shaped. Two facts prevent a stack war: Table Read and agent engines are UI-agnostic with zero rendering code and one event protocol; the app contract manifest plus mount is renderer-agnostic so an app folder may bundle its own library. Decision: shell and editor shelf-class surfaces stay vanilla TS plus DOM; every app folder has renderer freedom; when Table Read and agent chat surfaces reach implementation their specs must include a renderer assessment with React on the table against streaming updates, virtualized long lists, deep interactive state webs, and component-ecosystem needs; if two or more criteria hold React is the default for that surface otherwise vanilla; engines never acquire a renderer dependency. Consequences: no restart of prior layers; two rendering idioms may coexist bounded by folders-as-schema; this is the standing answer that React is decided per-surface at spec time. Note ADR-008 later supersedes the deferral of chat-surface choice while keeping the engine rule.

sections.title: Context
sections.summary: Shell and then-current Library Workbench Press Settings setup surfaces were hand-built vanilla TS plus DOM with five runtime dependencies and one compiled exe. Roadmap also promises chat-shaped surfaces: M4 Table Read conversational interview and agent system packages agent REPL test chat with Studio later at M6. Chat runtimes are classically React-shaped for streaming state and live lists, and comparable apps RoleCall Marinara Lumiverse frontend render chat with React 19. Two facts avoid a stack war: Table Read spec locks the engine as UI-agnostic with zero rendering code and one event protocol shared by CLI and Studio; agent packages follow the same rule so studio may not own private engine capabilities; renderer choice never touches engine design. App contract of manifest plus mount is renderer-agnostic; an app folder may bundle its own rendering library and the shell neither knows nor cares.

sections.title: Decision
sections.summary: Shell and editor shelf-class surfaces stay vanilla TS plus DOM because form and card complexity does not justify a framework runtime. Every app folder has renderer freedom: bundling a framework inside one app is an add not a rewrite and needs no shell change. When Table Read and agent chat surfaces reach implementation their specs must include a renderer assessment against sustained streaming updates, long virtualized lists, deep interactive state webs, and concrete component-ecosystem needs, with React explicitly on the table. If two or more criteria hold, default for that surface is React with Bun-native TSX baked into the exe; otherwise vanilla, with the event protocol keeping a later swap cheap. Engines never acquire a renderer dependency under any outcome.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.summary: No restart scenario exists: converter, canonical model, engines, shell, editors, and tokens CSS serve both renderer outcomes unchanged. The repo may eventually carry two rendering idioms isolated per app folder; that cost is accepted and bounded by folders-as-schema. This ADR is the standing answer to whether Studio should be React: the question is only ever asked per-surface with written criteria at the moment the surface is specced.
